evals.prompt: Our checkout E2E suite hasn't failed in three months. It costs CI minutes every run. Should we delete it?
evals.expected_output: No. A test that never fails is a safety net, not dead weight; it is what lets the team refactor and bump dependencies without silent breakage. Judge it by whether it covers a core workflow and keeps the feedback loop fast, not by bugs caught.

evals.prompt: Management wants a ranking of our test suites by number of bugs caught last quarter to decide which to invest in.
evals.expected_output: Reframe: rank by release confidence instead. Report feedback loop, suite reliability, release cadence, and production escape rate per suite; bug count on CI mostly reflects what developers did not catch locally.

evals.prompt: CI takes 12 minutes, we had 2 flaky re-runs out of 40 runs this month, deploys went from weekly to daily, and zero hotfixes since. What's our release confidence?
evals.expected_output: release_confidence: high. Feedback loop 12 minutes within target, suite reliability 95% above threshold, cadence rose with escape rate flat at zero, so all three questions are answered yes with evidence.

should_trigger: Is our automation suite actually worth the CI cost, and how confident should we be shipping Friday?
